slide.title: Every provider exchange has an owned lifetime
slide.takeaway: Capture, route and encode synthetic provider responses; abort sockets and gated iterators during cleanup.

item.label: Request contract
item.description: Raw HTTP and normalized request/tool observations retain provider identities. Request capture does not infer ACP session IDs or process input.

item.label: Routing and delivery
item.description: The session owns listener, route precedence, held handlers, waits, response transcript and the failure ledger. Unknown requests never fall through to live model providers.

item.label: Provider codecs
item.description: Separate codecs decode actual offered tool schemas/results and encode controlled text, tool calls, scripted HTTP errors and streaming terminal frames. Tool execution stays with the real consumer integration.

item.label: Bounded cleanup
item.description: Disconnect/dispose aborts delivery and held request work, rejecting waits and removing session configuration. User callbacks remain cooperative JavaScript; stopping network work cannot cancel arbitrary side effects.

item.label: A held user gate cannot hold the listener open
item.description: Network cleanup stops waiting for the producer.
item.body: A consumer generator can await forever. Disposal races network work against abort instead of waiting for that generator; sockets close, but arbitrary user-code side effects still require consumer cleanup.
